alg-hedge:
## Definition

Let $N,T\ge1$ be integers, let $[N]=\{1,\ldots,N\}$ be the expert set, and let $\epsilon>0$. At each round $t=1,\ldots,T$, a finite loss vector $\ell_t=(\ell_t(1),\ldots,\ell_t(N))\in[0,\infty)^N$ is revealed after the learner's choice. Initialize $W_1(i)=1$ for every $i\in[N]$. At round $t$, set
$$x_t(i):=\frac{W_t(i)}{\sum_{j=1}^{N}W_t(j)},\qquad i\in[N],$$
draw a measurable expert choice $I_t\in[N]$ with $\mathbb P(I_t=i)=x_t(i)$, and play $I_t$. After observing the whole vector $\ell_t$, update
$$W_{t+1}(i):=W_t(i)\exp(-\epsilon\ell_t(i)),\qquad i\in[N].$$
The output is the distributions $x_1,\ldots,x_T$, the sampled choices $I_1,\ldots,I_T$, and the final weights. Every factor $\exp(-\epsilon\ell_t(i))$ is a positive finite real; from the positive finite initial weights it follows by induction that every normalizing denominator is positive and finite. The protocol assumes a probability space carrying the stated measurable draws; no probability-space construction is claimed.
alg-online-gradient-descent:
## Definition

Let $d,T\ge1$ be integers, let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let $D,G\ge0$ be finite real bounds such that $\|u-v\|_2\le D$ for all $u,v\in K$ and $\|g_t\|_2\le G$. Supply an initial point $x_1\in K$. At each round $t=1,\ldots,T$, the learner plays $x_t$ and then receives the full loss function $f_t$ or the prescribed vector $g_t$. The smooth branch takes $f_t:U_t\to\mathbb R$ differentiable and convex on an open convex set $U_t\supseteq K$, with $g_t=\nabla f_t(x_t)$. The nonsmooth branch takes a convex function $f_t:C_t\to\mathbb R$ on a convex set $C_t\supseteq K$ and a supplied $g_t\in\partial f_t(x_t)$, where $\partial f_t(x_t)$ consists of vectors $g$ satisfying $f_t(y)\ge f_t(x_t)+\langle g,y-x_t\rangle$ for every $y\in C_t$; require explicitly that this inequality holds for every $u\in K$.

If $D=0$ or $G=0$, set $x_{t+1}=x_t$ at every round. If $D,G>0$, assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the metric projection. Set $\eta_t=D/(G\sqrt t)$, put $y_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_tg_t$, and set $x_{t+1}=P_K(y_{t+1})$, the unique point of $K$ minimizing Euclidean distance to $y_{t+1}$. Return the decisions $x_1,\ldots,x_T$. For random inputs, assume $x_1$ and each supplied $g_t$ are measurable; the nonexpansive projection map is continuous, so each projected update remains measurable.
thm-hedge-static-regret:
## Statement

Let $N,T\ge1$ be integers and let $\epsilon>0$. Let $\ell_t(i)\ge0$ be a finite real loss for every $t\in\{1,\ldots,T\}$ and $i\in[N]=\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Run Hedge with $W_1(i)=1$, $x_t(i)=W_t(i)/\sum_{j=1}^N W_t(j)$, measurable draws $I_t$ satisfying $\mathbb P(I_t=i)=x_t(i)$, and updates $W_{t+1}(i)=W_t(i)\exp(-\epsilon\ell_t(i))$. Assume the entire loss-vector sequence is fixed before the learner's random choices. For every fixed expert $i^\star\in[N]$, writing $\ell_t^{(2)}(i)=\ell_t(i)^2$, one has
$$
\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^N x_t(i)\ell_t(i)\le\sum_{t=1}^T\ell_t(i^\star)+\epsilon\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^N x_t(i)\ell_t^{(2)}(i)+\frac{\log N}{\epsilon},
$$
where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

If every loss lies in $[0,1]$ and $N\ge2$, choosing $\epsilon=\sqrt{\log N/T}$ gives expected static regret at most $2\sqrt{T\log N}$:
$$
\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^T\ell_t(I_t)-\min_{i\in[N]}\sum_{t=1}^T\ell_t(i)\right]\le2\sqrt{T\log N}.
$$
For $N=1$, the expected static regret is $0$.
thm-online-gradient-descent-regret:
## Statement

Let $d,T\ge1$ be integers, let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let $D,G\ge0$ be finite bounds such that $\|u-v\|_2\le D$ for all $u,v\in K$ and $\|g_t\|_2\le G$ for every round. Supply $x_1\in K$. On each round, either $f_t$ is differentiable and convex on an open convex neighborhood of $K$ and $g_t=\nabla f_t(x_t)$, or $f_t:C_t\to\mathbb R$ is convex on a convex set $C_t\supseteq K$ and a vector $g_t\in\partial f_t(x_t)$ is supplied with $f_t(u)\ge f_t(x_t)+\langle g_t,u-x_t\rangle$ explicitly required for every $u\in K$; here $\partial f_t(x_t)$ is the set of vectors satisfying that supporting inequality for every point of $C_t$. Run projected online gradient descent with $\eta_t=D/(G\sqrt t)$ when $D,G>0$, and with the no-op branch $x_{t+1}=x_t$ if $D=0$ or $G=0$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice only when $D,G>0$. For every realization satisfying these hypotheses and every $u\in K$,
$$\sum_{t=1}^T\bigl(f_t(x_t)-f_t(u)\bigr)\le\frac32DG\sqrt T.$$
If $D=0$ or $G=0$, this sum is nonpositive. Whenever the finite-horizon loss sum attains a finite minimum on $K$, the static regret, defined as $\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(x_t)-\min_{u\in K}\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(u)$, is therefore at most $\frac32DG\sqrt T$.
